thread:
elen: Observed a consistent delta where invoice_preview token totals are higher than ledger for several tenants after we rolled out the new request-fingerprint algorithm this morning. Preview shows ~18% higher on high-throughput routes.

harry: Do we have examples? Which pipelines compute fingerprints?

elen: Preview aggregator is showing duplicate-attribution spikes. Ledger final has deduped correctly. Sample pair for same logical request:

preview event (shadow topic):
{ req_id: "req_XYZ_1001", tenant: "evergreen", tokens: 256, fingerprint: "fp_v2_abc123", received_at: "2026-03-20T11:02:01Z" }

ledger raw event (ledger-ingest):
{ req_id: "req_XYZ_1001", tenant: "evergreen", tokens: 256, fingerprint: "fp_v1_9z7", ingested_at: "2026-03-20T11:02:02Z" }

sofia: Aha. We shipped the fingerprint change (v1 -> v2) in edge proxies earlier; preview cluster started ingesting fingerprint_v2 from the shadow topic, but ledger-ingest still uses v1 because it runs a compatibility step that falls back to a stable fingerprint if v2 present. The problem: preview dedupe key is fingerprint (it was used to collapse retries historically), ledger dedupes on req_id and canonical fingerprint mapping, so when edge retries produced two events with same req_id but different fingerprint flavors, preview treated them as separate requests and double-counted.

matt: Why did retry produce different fingerprints for same req_id? The new fingerprint incorporates request body canonicalization order that isn't stable across proxies when header ordering differs. The client retry path sometimes re-orders headers via gateway; v1 was tolerant, v2 is stricter. So same logical request got different fingerprint_v2 across hops. Ledger dedupe by req_id caught it, preview didn't.

elen: Quick numbers: query run across preview_events for last 6h shows ~42k events where req_id appears >1 with differing fingerprint values and summed tokens > ledger by ~1.2M tokens. Affected tenants are high-volume ones: evergreen, orbit-llc, skyline.

harry: Proposed immediate mitigation: revert preview aggregator to dedupe primarily on req_id (fallback to fingerprint if req_id missing), and treat fingerprint as metadata only. We can then migrate everyone to a canonical fingerprint scheme in a coordinated rollout.

sofia: Agree. Also add metric dedupe.key_mismatch_rate (ratio of same req_id with >1 fingerprint) and an alert when >0.1% over 5m. That would have flagged the mismatch sooner.

matt: Long-term fix: standardize fingerprint implementation in metering-contracts, ensure fingerprint generation is idempotent across gateway hops (normalize header ordering and canonicalize JSON body deterministically), and add unit tests that replicate retry/reorder scenarios.

elen: Backfill plan: run a replay on shadow topic for the 6h window and collapse events by req_id, emitting corrected preview rows with reconciled tokens. Owners: @harry patch preview-aggregator to prefer req_id dedupe and deploy canary; @sofia add metric + alert and update dashboard; @matt own fingerprint-contract and canonicalization tests + coordinate rollout with edge teams; @elen run the backfill and produce reconciliation report.

dev-bot: deploy-canary: preview-aggregator v6.4.2 -> v6.4.3 triggered by harry at 6976543235

billing-bot: Note: Ledger is authoritative for billing. No invoices will be changed. If backfill touches ledger correction topics we must route through billing-ops for review. For previews we can emit corrected "reconciled" snapshots.

harry: Canary looks healthy for 7m; dedupe by req_id dropped duplicate rate in canary cluster from 0.82% -> 0.02%. Will promote unless we see regressions in 20m.

sofia: I pushed dedupe.key_mismatch_rate metric and added a dashboard card showing top tenants with mismatches. Alert rule ready to enable post-deploy.

matt: I'll put up a PR in metering-contracts that defines fingerprint_v2 canonicalization steps and add a compatibility spec so rolling upgrades don't cause divergences. Plan to coordinate with edge at 24h notice.

elen: Running backfill job now. Will post a reconciliation summary with tenant-level diffs and sample traces so support can respond to customers if they ask.

harry: Good work team. Once promoted, let's schedule a short retro to tighten the rollout playbook for any future fingerprint or dedupe-key changes.
